parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, border/facility rule or police targeting is documented, and the same-sex statute is secondary per rubric, with no documented enforcement against trans visitors. But there is no operative visitor protection or recourse: criminalised same-sex conduct, official/religious hostility, significant stigma, people remaining closeted or leaving, banned LGBTI registration, and no anti-discrimination protections. Dated 2015 killings and a 2019 LGBT-wide health survey are not current trans-specific prevalence. Thin trans evidence resolves from these structural signals toward elevated risk, below administrative-friction jurisdictions with working remedies.

entry_documents.exposure: Same-sex conduct criminalised; no legal gender recognition so foreign passport read as issued. No documented border practice for mismatched presentation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch status is uncertain; if questioned, criminal law and lack of protections could be invoked, but no documented visitor enforcement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific detention, custody-placement or forced-examination practice sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented investigative pathway; do not infer detention practice from same-sex statute alone.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward or facility-access rule for visitors sourced.

care_services.exposure: No broad SOGI health protection; assessment notes refusal risk. 2019 LGBT-wide 59% disrespect/30% denial is dated and not trans-specific, given no current weight.
care_services.protection: 2013 SRH policy requires services regardless of orientation; 2012 HIV counselling/testing extended to same-sex couples; 2021 guidelines name LGBT people at higher GBV risk.
care_services.interaction: Inclusive policy sits beneath unchanged criminal law with no discrimination remedy, limiting operative protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Sodomy/common-law criminalisation for men and women; officials and religious/traditional actors criticise same-sex conduct; 2012 minister rejected protection law; advocacy registration refused on morality.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional association/privacy/expression recognised in 2022; 2023 supreme court voided registrar refusal per source; broadcasting guidelines bar incitement on orientation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile law and official framing coexist with paper constitutional/policy protections and police-escorted 2018 Pride, but commerce ministry still refuses registration.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No visitor/minor-specific rule sourced; resident same-sex adoption ban is not a visitor exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling couple in a same-sex relationship would fall under criminal law; no minor-specific interaction documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Significant stigma and fear of rejection; two 2015/earlier killings in one town are individual dated incidents, not a rate or pattern. No trans-specific violence rate sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2018 Pride with 2,000 attendees was police-escorted; 2021 virtual Pride without incident; welcoming church reopened 2018.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Tolerated public visibility does not offset absence of legal recourse if harassment escalates.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No broad SOGI anti-discrimination remedy in education, health, housing, employment; no registered national advocacy body; civic space severely closed (Not Free 17/100).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have recognised constitutional rights and voided one registration refusal, but remedy for a visitor facing discrimination or violence is not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Border practice, facility rules, detention placement and later registration applications remain unresolved as stated in dossier.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-B risk is not shown: no documented routine police stops, passport confiscation, fines or district exclusion of trans visitors. The dossier lacks 0.35's organised visitor-facing enforcement.

Higher risk than 0.55-B: that anchor has administrative denial plus written reasons, appeal desk and consular notification. Here there is no documented visitor remedy, plus criminalisation, official hostility and no protections.
Well below 0.75-C: that anchor accepts matching markers, trains officers, and provides tribunal, counsel and compensation. None of those operative visitor protections is documented here.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: inclusive health/GBV policy and court-recognised constitutional rights, plus tolerated Pride, are not operative traveller protections against the documented criminal law, stigma, closed registration and absence of anti-discrimination recourse. No trans-specific universal exposure or organised targeting is documented, preventing a severe-tier rating; no documented protections prevent a reduced-risk rating. Uncertainty on border, facilities and detention is stated, not treated as safety, keeping the score in elevated risk.
